In 725 a speaker recounts a change in how he tends his own body after discovering the divine within. reason: In 2414 the repeated condition for dispensing with recitation and breath practices is the mind's rectitude. In 2635 an address to the woman of wisdom moves from the inward guru to a question about firing a substance. Both turn attention inward, but the question supplies neither a judgment about breath nor the condition stated in 2414.

In 295 the speaker addresses the mind and names remembrance of the divine feet as its medicine after raising the prospect of escaping death. In 725 the speaker tends the body because the highest one dwells there. Both bring devotion into intimate relation with bodily life, but 725 makes no promise about death and 295 prescribes remembrance.

In 127 a speaker longs to move free of caste distinctions in accordance with the cited teaching. In 355 an impersonal maxim defines knowledge as discerning the true substance of whatever one encounters. Its scope could include received teachings, but it singles out no scripture, while the first speaker expressly invokes one.
